title: Uldaman
body: Uldaman lies buried beneath the northern Badlands, a vault of the titans far older than any dwarven hold, its halls and stairways cut from the living rock on a scale no mortal mason ever attempted. The dwarves of Ironforge broke into it, and their excavation still scars the outer halls: empty camps, cold cookfires, chests left behind in haste. They did not keep it. The Stonevault troggs boiled up out of the depths in numbers no dig crew could hold back, and they swarm the old tunnels still, while the Shadowforge clan of the Dark Iron dwarves digs behind barricades of its own. Deeper in, past troggs and diggings alike, the vault keeps guardians of its own, figures of living stone that stand as still as statues. Explorers come looking for lost companions and the secrets of the makers of the world, and others for whatever the fleeing and the fallen left behind.

title: The Common Halls
body: The first halls of Uldaman, cut deep into the cliffs beyond the Maker's Terrace, still show the dwarves who dug here. Their chests stand in the Common Halls, north and south, abandoned when the troggs came. Shadowforge diggers and surveyors work the halls now, guarded by ruffians and obsidian golems, and Stonevault cave hunters prowl the tunnels with their nets. Clusters of magenta fungus caps grow along the walls, and a jostled cluster spews poison spores.

parts.body: Somewhere among the Shadowforge in these halls walks Magregan Deepshadow. He carries an amulet taken from the old prisoner the Dark Irons dragged here, and anyone who means to help the prisoner must win it back from him before it leads his clan to what they are digging for.

When it came back to him he felt complete again. Some dwarves treasure the luster of metal and some the glint of gems, he said, but a Stoutarm without a treasured stein in hand is hardly a Stoutarm at all.

title: The Hall of the Keepers
body: Past the gate of the vault proper opens its first great hall, the Hall of the Keepers, and the Stonevault troggs hold it in force. Rockchewers fly into a frenzy when wounded, and oracles raise shields of lightning, healing wards and spouts of lava for their kin. From the hall, ways lead off into side digs and deeper chambers. In one corner, where the troggs pay them no mind, lie the remains of a paladin, left where he fell.

parts.body: At the far end of the hall, where it opens on the next chamber, Revelosh stood among the troggs. He fought with lightning, hurling bolts at single foes and chains of it that leapt from one to the next, and he fell there all the same.

title: The Halls of Living Stone
body: Beyond the halls the troggs hold, the vault grows quieter, but it is not empty. Its side caves crawl with cleft scorpids, and shrike bats and basilisks nest in the passages. Past them lies the Temple Hall, and figures of living stone called earthen keep it and the ways around it: rocksmashers who strike with crushing force and sculptors who wreathe themselves in fire and buffet their foes with flame. Stone stewards shake the ground beneath intruders' feet. The stone folk do not speak, and they do not let anyone pass.

parts.body: In a side cave crawling with cleft scorpids hides Annora, an enchanter. Whoever clears the creatures from her hiding place earns her undying gratitude: she had begun to think she might have to hide out forever. What brought her so deep she does not say, but she has kept her craft, and she will teach it to those who ask.

parts.body: Greatest of the Temple Hall's guardians was the Ancient Stone Keeper, a great figure of living rock. When intruders reached it, it called up whirling storms of sand to fight at its side and pounded on among them, until at last it was broken and fell still in the hall it had kept.

title: Echomok Cavern
body: Echomok Cavern lies at the vault's back door, where a rough passage leads out of the ruins to the open Badlands, the one that opens on Dustwind Gulch. The Shadowforge hold it now. Their relic hunters search the cavern for whatever the titans left, withering their foes with shadow and silencing their spells while they mend their own wounded, and geologists among them lash out with flame. A heavy door, the Echomok Door, stands at the cavern's edge.

parts.body: Something older than the Dark Irons stood in the cavern: the Obsidian Sentinel, a construct of black volcanic glass. Struck, it turned spells back on those who cast them, sprayed splinters of its own obsidian, and shed shards of itself that came to life and joined the fight. For all of that, it shattered at last on the cavern floor.

title: The Hall of the Crafters
body: In the eastern reaches of Uldaman lies the Hall of the Crafters, grander than the halls before it, and the stone folk who keep it are stronger: earthen stonebreakers who strike with crushing blows and stonecarvers who wrap themselves in fire. On its upper floor stands an altar, and around it four stone keepers wait, as still as statues, before a closed temple door. Its lower floor opens on a vast chamber where rows of stone figures stand silent, as still as the keepers above.

parts.body: Whoever called upon the altar woke the keepers, and they shook off their stillness one at a time. Each trampled its foes and then, as it fell, blew itself apart, and as each one died the next stirred to take its place. With the keepers' fall the temple door beyond them stood open, and the way led on.

title: Ironaya
body: Ironaya is a guardian of Uldaman, a towering figure of iron sealed away in a hidden chamber behind the great carved Seal of Khaz'mul. A keystone stands before the seal, and it will not turn for just anyone: only the right key unlocks it. Those who open the way find that the chamber has not been left unguarded, and that its keeper has not forgotten what she was set there to protect.

parts.body: When the keystone turned, the seal took long moments to grind open, and then Ironaya stirred and strode out with a warning: none may steal the secrets of the Makers. She swept her foes with arcing blows, struck them flying across the hall and stamped the ground to stun all around her. In the end she fell, and the hidden chamber lay open to explore.

title: Archaedas
body: Archaedas, the Ancient Stone Watcher, sits in Khaz'goroth's Seat, the great chamber beneath the Hall of the Crafters, a giant of living stone seated in silence. Around him stand rows of stone dwarves, custodians, hallshapers and guardians, as still as he is, and behind him the door of the Ancient Vault stays shut. Before him stands an altar. Whatever lies in the vault, he is its last guard, and calling upon that altar is how anyone wakes him.

parts.body: He woke with a roar, demanding who dared awaken Archaedas, who dared the wrath of the Makers. He shook the ground beneath his foes and woke the stone dwarves around him a few at a time, and as he weakened he bade his servants awake and defend the discs, then called the vault warders, his brothers, to his side. Any foe who fell he named a reckless mortal. When Archaedas fell, every servant he had woken was gone with him, and the door of the Ancient Vault opened.

title: Galgann Firehammer
body: Galgann Firehammer is the Dark Iron master of Dig Three, the Shadowforge dig deep in the ruins, a barricaded camp where sharpshooters, darkcasters, archaeologists and geologists work and stand guard around him. Close by his post an ancient tablet lies among the clan's diggings. He is a master of fire, and he does not take kindly to strangers in his dig.

parts.body: Galgann met intruders with an oath by Thaurissan's beard and ordered his dwarves to slay them. He wreathed his foes in fire, lashing and searing them with flame, bursting into a nova of fire and laying on them a curse that made the flames bite deeper. He fell among his diggings all the same, and Dig Three lost its master.

title: Grimlok
body: Of all the troggs that swarm Uldaman, none stands above Grimlok, chieftain of the Stonevault. He keeps to the Stone Vault deep in the ruins with his brawlers and fire-hurling geomancers about him and jadespine basilisks crouched nearby. He is no common brute: like the oracles of his tribe he calls on the power of storm and earth, and he has made himself master of the deep halls he holds.

parts.body: Me Grimlok, king, he bellowed as the fight began, and he fought like a shaman of his tribe, hurling lightning that leapt from foe to foe, shrinking a foe to a fraction of his strength and planting a totem in the ground. Wounded, he whipped himself into a bloodlust, and over every foe who fell he roared Die, die. The king of the troggs fell at last in his own vault.

title: Baelog
body: Baelog is a dwarf of Ironforge who keeps a camp in a side dig off the first hall of the vault, with troggs on every side. With him are two companions, Eric, called the Swift, and Olaf, who bears a great shield. The camp has a fire to sit by, a stout chest and a journal, and the three look as though they have been there a long while. They are loyal to Ironforge and the Alliance, and any of the Horde who walk into their camp find three seasoned dwarves raising their weapons against them.

parts.body: The dwarves did not give up their camp quietly. Eric came on at a rush, Olaf slammed foes senseless with his shield, and Baelog struck hard and fast, three veterans fighting side by side. In the end Baelog himself fell in the camp he had kept so long, and the camp fell quiet.

title: The Platinum Discs
body: Beyond the door that opened when the vault's last guard fell lies a treasure chamber, and its centerpieces are four huge platinum discs adorned with sigils of no known origin. A hand laid on them tingles. At the touch the image of a great stone watcher springs up beside them, the Lore Keeper of Norgannon, and offers its salutations: it is a keeper of knowledge, and the record of the Creators' work for this world is stored here, it says, in the Discs of Norgannon. Then it waits beside the discs, ready to be asked.

parts.body: The stone watcher would not part with its record lightly. Only when the visitor had heard all it had to tell, of the earthen, of the troggs and of the dwarves, would it let the discs be touched again. Then a faint, brief hum sounded within them, and the watcher declared the discs synthesized: one more touch, and a copy would be the visitor's own to keep.
sources: quest 2278 completion text (satisfy the data assimilation prerequisite; fully explore the information within this repository first) and reward text (now that you have learned about the history of the Earthen, the troggs, and the dwarves; a faint, brief hum; access once more to receive your personal copy)

parts.body: At the next touch a strange grinding sounded from inside the discs, and a pack grew suddenly heavier: in it lay a miniature version of the discs. The sages of Thunder Bluff, historians known throughout the Horde, would surely know what to make of such a thing.
sources: quest 2280 description (grinding noise; miniature version of the discs in your backpack; the sages of Thunder Bluff, known throughout the Horde)

title: The Shattered Necklace
body: Somewhere in Uldaman turns up a tarnished necklace whose tarnish cannot hide its craftsmanship, intricate and plainly magical. It has been shattered: its setting stands empty where three gems once sat. On its underside is the faint imprint of the city seal of Ironforge, and below the seal three tiny engraved letters, TdK. Whatever the necklace is worth, and whatever it has to do with these ruins, the place to start is with whoever made it, and the seal and the initials point the way.

parts.body: The paladin who carried the necklace last was found in the vault, or what remained of him, and his journal with him. After much effort he had learned where all three gems had gone. The Shadowforge hid the ruby in their barricaded dig as they battled the troggs for the ruins; the troggs stashed the topaz in an urn close to some unexpected dwellers, dwarves of the Alliance; and Grimlok, the trogg leader, kept the sapphire for himself.
sources: quest 2201 description and objectives (the paladin's journal; the ruby in a barricaded Shadowforge area; the topaz in an urn in one of the trogg areas near some Alliance dwarves; the sapphire claimed by Grimlok); quest_template_addon 2201 PrevQuestID 2200
creature 6912 Remains of a Paladin (questgiver of 2201)
gameobjects 113757 Shadowforge Cache (21,414), 125477 Conspicuous Urn (-351,83, beside Baelog's camp)

parts.body: With all three gems in hand, the finder called on Talvash through his phial of scrying, and the jeweler's image rose from the water of the bowl: still alive, he marveled, and he begged not to have a charge wasted just to chat, for those things are not cheap. The gems were the right ones. But the necklace had no strength left in it and needed a power source, and the biggest, baddest construct in Uldaman ought to have one. What came of it is the jeweler's own tale.
sources: quest 2201 completion text (Talvash's image comes into focus from the waters of the scrying bowl; still alive; don't waste a charge just to chat) and reward text (those are the three gems; you need a strong power source; the necklace has no more oomph to give)

parts.body: Anyone careless enough to lose the phial heard about it. Phials of scrying do not grow on trees, Talvash complained, and he demanded a mana potion, a piece of coal and some sweet nectar to make another. When they arrived he admitted he had a spare all along, and that the makings would do for the next one, when that was lost too.
sources: quest 3375 description and reward text (those phials don't grow on trees; a mana potion, coal and sweet nectar; I lied, I had another phial; enough to make you another when you lose that too)

title: Necklace Recovery
body: In Orgrimmar, Dran Droffers of Droffers and Son Salvage has heard a tale worth silver. Some idiot paladin died at the Uldaman dig site in the Badlands not long ago, and he had a very valuable necklace on him, said to carry three large gems: a ruby, a sapphire and a topaz. The Droffers want it. It may be damaged, Dran allows, but that is neither here nor there, for they will fix whatever scratches it has, and they are paying top silver to whoever has the guts to go and get it.

parts.body: The necklace came out of Uldaman, but its gems were gone. Dran was furious, swearing that even his son Malton could see it, and though he allowed that the finder might not have stolen them, the necklace was worthless without them. The gems had to be somewhere in Uldaman, he reasoned, and if the paladin's corpse had not been stripped clean, they might still be on him.
sources: quest 2283 reward text (this necklace is missing the gems; even Malton could see the gems are gone; worthless without those gems)
quest 2284 description (those gems are still in Uldaman somewhere; maybe you'll find the corpse of the paladin)

parts.body: The paladin's remains lay in the vault. He had no gems on him, only a journal, most of its pages stained with dried blood, and what could still be read was written in the tongue of humans, gibberish to the finder. It would have to be translated, and the nearest place that might have someone able to do it was Kargath, the Horde outpost in the Badlands.
sources: quest 2284 reward text (the remains of the paladin; his journal; dried blood; written in the native tongue of the humans; you will need the book translated)
quest 2318 description (the closest location that might have someone is the Kargath outpost)

parts.body: At Kargath the troll Jarkal Mossmeld was waiting, and he already knew what the finder carried and why: it is his job to know such things. He alone could translate the journal, he said, and he had a better offer than the Droffers. Let him borrow the necklace to study, so that he could learn to make such pieces himself, and he would translate the journal in return. No one else would be the wiser.
sources: quest 2318 reward text (I know you seek my gift of tongues; I'm the only one who can translate it; a better offer than Dran Droffers)
quest 2338 description (Droffers and Son Salvage aren't smart enough to restore the magic; let me borrow it; no one else will be the wiser)
creature 6868 Jarkal Mossmeld in Kargath (badlands.json 301 names him only)

parts.body: True to his word, Jarkal cast a spell over the journal and it could be read. The dwarves had hidden the ruby, the troggs the topaz, and a trogg named Grimlok had the sapphire. And there was something Dran did not know: the necklace needed a power source to work again, and Jarkal advised going as deep into Uldaman as possible and killing whatever construct was the strongest there.
sources: quest 2338 reward text (a spell to translate the human tongue; a troll of my word)
quest 2339 description and objectives (dwarves hid the ruby, troggs the topaz, Grimlok has the sapphire; a power source; kill whatever construct is the strongest)

parts.body: With the gems and the power source before him, Jarkal studied them with an incantation of his own and declared himself finished with the necklace: he could copy its making. The necklace and its gems would go to Orgrimmar as promised, but the power source he kept, for it was what would bring the magic back.
sources: quest 2339 reward text (I am confident I can duplicate the construction process; analyze those gems) and completion text (I will be keeping the power source; the thing that will make the necklace work)

parts.body: Jarkal sent the finder on to Orgrimmar with a warning to keep quiet about their deal, hinting at a surprise on the way back. There Dran Droffers checked everything twice and three times over, kept the bag as well, and crowed that the necklace would be the firm's greatest haul yet. He paid the agreed fee and told the finder to beat it, and as he and Malton began squabbling over their new salvage, half the deal was done.
sources: quest 2340 description (just keep your mouth shut about our deal; I might have a wonderful surprise for you)
quest 2340 completion and reward text (double and triple checking; mind if we keep the bag; our greatest haul yet; here's your fee; beat it)
quest 2341 description (Dran and Malton Droffers begin to squabble over their new salvage; half of the deal is now complete)

parts.body: The other half waited in Kargath. The power source had exceeded every hope Jarkal had for it: he had made one necklace for himself and one for his partner in the deal, with enough left over for at least three more, and they would fetch a fine fee with Droffers and Son Salvage none the wiser.
sources: quest 2341 reward text (the power source exceeded every expectation; made both you and me a necklace; enough left over to make at least three more; Droffers and Son Salvage none the wiser)
quest 2283 description (an idiot paladin who died at the Uldaman dig site; a very valuable necklace with a ruby, a sapphire and a topaz; top silver; we'll fix whatever scratches)
